title: Welcome and Table of Contents
summary: What SS1 Mathematics Third Term covers (mensuration and statistics), how to use the notes, and a map of every unit.

p: Welcome to the last term of SS1 Mathematics. This term has two big themes. The first is mensuration: measuring lengths, areas and volumes, from arcs and sectors of circles to the surface area and volume of solids such as cylinders, cones, pyramids and frustums. The second is statistics: collecting data, putting it in tables and showing it in graphs such as bar charts, histograms, pie charts and frequency polygons.

Both themes are very useful: engineers, builders, farmers, nurses, businesses and governments all use them. They also carry many marks in WAEC, NECO and JAMB, so take your time over every worked example.

Read each unit slowly and study the pictures. Try the worked examples yourself before you read the solution. Learn the formulas and write them in your notebook. At the end of each unit, do the activity and the practice questions. The practice questions do not count towards a mark; they help you check your understanding. Answer them all correctly to complete the unit.

You need a scientific calculator, a ruler, compasses, a protractor and graph paper. The midterm examination is in Week 5 and there is a break in Week 7, so there are no new units for those weeks. Use them to revise.

p: Draw a diagram for every mensuration problem and label the sizes. Always check whether a formula needs the vertical height or the slant height. Keep the units: length in cm, area in cm² and volume in cm³. In statistics, choose the right graph for the data type, label the axes and give each graph a title.
